g.text: Swizzle<3,4,3> on a shared memory byte offset
bits 9..7 = row r in the 8-row atom
bits 6..4 = 16-byte chunk c in the 128-byte row
MBase = 4: the low 4 bits never change,
SShift = 3: the source bits sit three
Where logical chunk c of row r is stored: physical chunk c XOR r
logical chunk c (bits 6..4 before the swizzle)
each row is 128 bytes = eight 16-byte chunks = one pass over the 32 banks
Reading logical chunk 0 of all eight rows
positions in their 128-byte rows, so eight
different bank groups and no conflict.
Without the swizzle the same read hits
physical chunk 0 in every row: the same
which is why operand buffers are
